result: FAILED — the test threw before it could write its own transcript, so this file was assembled by hand from the two runs' captured output and Playwright's own error text.
finding: Steps (a) and (b) pass: open, then hello, then change (naming the session) all arrive within their windows. Step (c) does NOT: after `server.kill('SIGKILL')`, no `error` event was observed by the browser's EventSource within the spec's 10000ms window, on either run. A manual reproduction (curl -N through the same vite proxy, same kill) shows why — the client's connection to the proxy never closes at all; curl still holds it open past the kill with zero further bytes. This is the silent-stall case the spec's own header names: the vite proxy is not propagating the black-smith process's TCP close to the client. The load-bearing tuple (error after kill, open/hello after restart) was NOT produced. This is a real finding about the proxy, not a flaky test — it reproduced identically across two separate runs (see `runs` below) and via a proxy-level `curl` probe outside Playwright entirely.

manualProbe.description: curl -N through vam's own vite proxy (http://127.0.0.1:5273/api/stream), black-smith killed with SIGKILL 3s in, curl left running with --max-time 20
manualProbe.observation: curl received `hello` and `change` frames, then zero further bytes and no connection close for the remainder of the 20s window — the proxy held the client socket open past the upstream's death.
